paragraphs: Swamiji described a scene from the oil mills of India. A bullock is harnessed to the mill and made to walk in circles to crush the oil-seed. A piece of wood sticks out from the yoke on its neck, and a wisp of straw is tied to the end of it.

The bullock wears a blindfold that lets it see only straight ahead. It spots the straw and stretches its neck to grab it, but the very act of stretching pushes the wood, and the straw, a little further away. So it tries again, and again, with the same result. It never gets the straw. It just keeps going round and round, hoping for the next bite, and all the while it is grinding out oil for someone else.

Swamiji said we are exactly like that bullock. Bound to nature, money, wealth, family and the rest, we keep chasing a wisp of straw that is really just a fantasy. Life after life we go round in circles, and we never actually get what we are looking for.
learn: Many of us run after the next goal, the next purchase or the next approval, only to find it slipping further away each time. Every so often, stop and ask: am I moving forward, or just walking in a circle with a blindfold on?
